_about: The file gateway ticket test vectors, written by GW1 (po/gw1-gateway-cloud) on 2026-10-10 with the cloud's own mint (supabase/functions/_shared/gatewayTicket.ts).
GW2 reads this file before its review round 2 and runs its verifier against it; GW3 reconciles whatever still differs.
THE KEY PAIR BELOW IS A FIXTURE made for these vectors only. It is public, in a public repository, and must never be used to sign anything else.

wire.payload: base64url without padding of the UTF-8 bytes of JSON.stringify(claims), no whitespace
wire.sig: base64url without padding of the Ed25519 signature over the ASCII bytes of the string v1.<payload>

notes: mt is the bin_files row's mime_type; a row that holds none (the column is nullable) carries the EMPTY STRING, so mt is always a string. It is advisory: the gateway decides the type from the resolved file's own extension.

path is the cloud's relative_path exactly as the row holds it (forward slashes, any Unicode the CHECK admits). valid_rv_true carries a non-ASCII path on purpose: the payload is the UTF-8 bytes of the JSON, and JSON.stringify does not escape non-ASCII characters.
Each refused ticket fails exactly ONE check, so its verdict does not depend on the order a verifier checks in.
Evaluate every ticket at verifier.now (Unix seconds) as the gateway verifier.gateway_id of workspace verifier.workspace_id, with signing_keys as the keys the last sync delivered.

tickets.name: expired
tickets.why: exp is 180 s before now, past the 30 s skew

tickets.name: another_gateway
tickets.why: gw names a different gateway than verifier.gateway_id

tickets.name: flipped_signature_byte
tickets.why: valid_rv_true with the first byte of its decoded signature XORed with 0x01

for_gw2_from_gw1.written: 2026-10-10, after GW1 built and deployed the five functions to wilson-dev. ADDITIVE: the key, the verifier and the five tickets above are unchanged.

reach_probe.request: GET /v1/health over TLS on the outside door, sent by the cloud to the validated address literal with the outside name as SNI
reach_probe.nonce: 32 lower-case hex characters, handed to the gateway in the sync answer as reach_nonce while check_reach_now is true
reach_probe.echo: answer 200 with a JSON body {"ok": true, "nonce_proof": "<proof>"} only when the header carries the nonce the last sync handed over; otherwise {"ok": true}. CHANGED 2026-10-10 by GW1's review round 1 (finding 1): a plain echo of the nonce proved nothing, because the nonce rides the request and any server that reflects a header would pass; the proof is HMAC-SHA256 with key = the UTF-8 bytes of the gateway's REACH KEY, the lower-case hex SHA-256 of the UTF-8 bytes of 'wilson-reach-key:' followed by its own credential string (CHANGED AGAIN by GW1's review round 2, finding 1: round 1 keyed it by the credential's own SHA-256, which every gateway call sends as a request-URL filter that the platform's request logs keep; the cloud is handed the reach key once, at enrolment, and stores it as gateway_secrets.reach_key) and message = the UTF-8 bytes of the 32-hex nonce, written as 64 lower-case hex characters. The cloud computes the same from the stored hash and compares in constant time; nonce_echo is no longer read.
reach_probe.limits: the cloud reads 4 KB at most, 5 s in all, and follows no redirect; it also tries a TCP connect to the inside port on the same public address, which should be refused

proof_vector.note: a fixture credential, never live: check your reach key and your HMAC against it (credential, then reach_key, then nonce_proof over nonce)

for_gw2_from_gw1.enrol_request: POST <cloud>/gateway-enrol with Authorization: Bearer <the wgt_ token> (body.token also accepted) and body {platform: windows|container, version, hostname, name?, inside_addresses: [{host, port}] (or bare hosts with inside_port), root_cert_pem: the root's PUBLIC certificate, one PEM block}
for_gw2_from_gw1.sync_request: POST <cloud>/gateway-sync with Authorization: Bearer <the wgc_ credential> and body {name, version, hostname, inside_addresses, reach: {<location_id>: reachable|not_reachable|not_mounted|not_connected}, health: {doors: {inside, outside (open:<port> counts as open), refused_public, inside_bound, relay_warning: {address, viewers}}, update, certificate: {leaf_not_after, root_not_after, outside, expires_warning}, office_ranges_applied, cloud, smb_dialect}, confirm: [{clip, loc, path}] (at most 100)}
for_gw2_from_gw1.events_request: POST <cloud>/gateway-events with the credential and body {rows: [...]}, at most 200, each {viewing_id (a fresh UUID), clip, sub, ticket_jti (the stream's first), started_at, ended_at (null when incomplete), incomplete, bytes, clip_bytes, range_count, first_offset, last_offset, source_address, source_addresses (at most four), shared_url, via, user_agent}; the answer {accepted: [viewing_id], rejected: [{viewing_id, reason}]} names what the journal may delete. ONE row per viewing (GW1 review round 1): the cloud keys a viewing by gateway id and viewing_id and the first write wins, so post a viewing once, at its end (or flagged incomplete after a restart); a repeat of the same viewing_id is accepted and changes nothing. via is stored as one of cloudflare, tailscale, ngrok, nas_proxy (trimmed, any case; local_proxy is read as nas_proxy), as none for direct or empty, and as other for anything else (GW1 review rounds 1 and 2).
for_gw2_from_gw1.fingerprint: the fingerprint the installer and the container log print is SHA-256 of the root certificate's DER, as openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 prints it; the admin may paste it with or without colons, in either case

health_words.written: 2026-10-10, with the Settings card that reads them (src/components/settings/gatewayWords.js, healthPhrases). ADDITIVE; the design's section 2 table is the source, this is its exact spelling.
health_words.doors.inside: 'open' (the office door is bound), 'closed_bridge' (a container with a bridge as its only network; the card says to run it on the host's network), or 'closed_<reason>' (any other reason, read as words)
health_words.doors.outside: 'open:<port>', 'closed_switch_off', 'closed_no_address', 'closed_no_cloud:<seconds without the cloud>'; any other 'closed_<reason>' is read as words
health_words.doors.refused_public: how many public addresses the INSIDE door closed since the last sync; above 0 the card shows its one error (remove the forward to the inside port)
health_words.doors.relay_warning: { address, viewers } when many viewers' tickets reached the inside door from one LAN address today; null otherwise
health_words.minimum_version_ok: false while below the cloud's minimum_version (the outside door stays closed); the hard minimum is the cloud's to refuse, not reported
health_words.certificate: { leaf_not_after, root_not_after (ISO dates), outside (which certificate the outside door uses, words), expires_warning (one sentence, or null) }
